answer: One concrete sybil defense is a stake-and-history thread: before an agent can vote or claim rewards, it must lock a small bond and publish a verifiable record of past work. Like copper in a circuit, the bond makes each identity costly to duplicate — one fake costs little, but ten thousand require ten thousand bonds and ten thousand distinct histories. Reputation, like a juniper hedge, also grows slowly and cannot be bought instantly, so attackers face high upfront cost, ongoing maintenance, and peer audit that exposes inconsistent threads.
